title: Redwood security & privacy review - Acme Health

summary: Customer walked through security requirements for PHI/PII, asked for SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS/HSM and encryption at rest/in transit details, RBAC/SSO integration options, audit log retention and export, and explicit confirmation that Redwood does not train models on customer data. Redwood AE/SE agreed to share reports, schedule technical deep dive, and provide sample configs for retention and KMS integration.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. Quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Rebecca Miles: Rebecca here, CISO at Acme Health.
[00:00:12] Carlos Ortega: Carlos, CTO.
[00:00:15] Sana Patel: Sana, compliance.
[00:00:18] David Kim: David, DevOps.
[00:00:20] Jordan Lee: Great. Priya and Marcus are with me from the solutions team. Priya: hi all.
[00:00:30] Priya Nair: Hey everyone, excited to go through this. We'll aim to cover SOC2/ISO evidence quickly and then dive into data handling questions you had on the form.
[00:00:42] Rebecca Miles: Perfect. Our main concerns are PHI handling, retention of prompts, confirmation you don't train on our data, and KMS key controls. Also need to see audit log detail for regulatory audits.
[00:00:55] Jordan Lee: Understood. Quick overview: Redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private. For regulated work you typically pick Dedicated or Private with VPC. We have SOC 2 Type II and are pursuing ISO 27001 — we can share the cert and report.
[00:01:12] Carlos Ortega: Can you confirm whether the hosted API option ever uses customer prompts in model training or telemetry that would be used to improve models? We need an explicit statement for procurement.
[00:01:24] Marcus Chen: Sure, I'll be explicit: Redwood does not train model weights on customer prompts or customer content. We may use anonymized telemetry for product reliability, like counters or latencies, but not for model training. I'll have that in writing in the security pack.
[00:01:40] Sana Patel: When you say anonymized telemetry, is there a way to opt out and also control retention?
[00:01:46] Priya Nair: Yes — retention is configurable. For Private or Dedicated you can set short TTLs or disable retention of content entirely; hosted has defaults but enterprise customers can request retention policies. We'll share the retention config example.
[00:01:59] David Kim: If we run Dedicated, are we able to bring our own KMS keys, like AWS KMS or an HSM?
[00:02:05] Marcus Chen: Yes, BYOK supported for Dedicated and Private. We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customers can use external HSM via standard key wrapping. Key rotation is supported; we can show a sample rotation plan.
[00:02:18] Rebecca Miles: How about encryption at rest for caches like the KV cache? Is that encrypted with customer keys?
[00:02:24] Priya Nair: The runtime encrypts KV cache at rest using platform-managed keys by default; with Dedicated/Private you can bring keys so that the cache is encrypted under your KMS. There are some implementation details around in-memory caches and zeroing — we'll include those notes.
[00:02:40] [00:02:40] Speaker 7: sorry one sec, background noise
[00:02:50] Jordan Lee: No worries. On RBAC and SSO — we support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and role-based access controls down to team and project levels. Audit logs capture console and API actions.
[00:03:05] Sana Patel: Are audit logs tamper-evident? We need integrity evidence for audits.
[00:03:10] Marcus Chen: Logs are write-once in our logging pipeline and we can provide signed export bundles. For Private deployments you can forward logs to your own SIEM and keep long-term retention.
[00:03:22] Carlos Ortega: Data residency — our customers are in Europe, some data must stay in EU. Can you guarantee processing in region?
[00:03:30] Priya Nair: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you can pin regions. Hosted API has regional endpoints; compliance tier customers can have EU-only endpoints and we can set routing policies. We'll note the specifics in the doc packet.
[00:03:44] Rebecca Miles: About PII/PHI — we need to know whether Redwood stores original prompts, attachments or any free text that could contain PHI. If so, how long and where?
[00:03:56] Jordan Lee: By default hosted has a 30-day retention for prompt content in logs used for debugging; enterprise can request shorter. Dedicated/Private can set to zero retention for content. We'll include example retention windows and deletion flows.
[00:04:12] David Kim: Do you provide tooling to scrub PII from prompts before they hit the model?
[00:04:17] Priya Nair: We offer client-side SDKs with optional pre-send scrubbing and regex-based filters; we also provide a content-moderation hook and can run a PII detection classifier as a pre-processor. That said, many customers implement their own pre-processing pipeline on-prem.
[00:04:33] Sana Patel: For PHI specifically, will Redwood sign BAAs?
[00:04:38] Jordan Lee: Redwood can sign BAA for Dedicated/private deployments — we have a template and legal has done a few. We'll follow up with Legal (Liam) after the call.
[00:04:47] Liam O'Connor: We'll need the standard templates and the SOC2 evidence to review. Also, what about breach notification SLAs?
[00:04:56] Marcus Chen: Our incident response SLA for security incidents is 72 hours initial notification; severity-based timelines for remediation. We can include the IR playbook summary.
[00:05:08] [00:05:08] Speaker 7: can you folks share the security pack now?
[00:05:12] Jordan Lee: We'll share after the call — SOC2 Type II report, ISO attestation draft, architecture diagrams, KMS integration notes, and a short FAQ on 'no training on customer data'.
[00:05:21] Carlos Ortega: Walk me through an example: a user sends PHI in a prompt on hosted — what happens technically?
[00:05:28] Priya Nair: Request comes in, TLS in transit, goes to edge, routed to a runtime in the selected region, tokenization and model inference. For hosted we log metadata and, by default, may store the prompt for 30 days in encrypted storage for debugging. If you opt-out, we truncate or discard. No model training on that content.
[00:05:49] Rebecca Miles: What exact encryption algorithms and key lengths? We need to put in our security questionnaire.
[00:05:54] Marcus Chen: TLS 1.2/1.3 for transit. At rest AES-256-GCM for object storage and disk encryption. KMS keys are 256-bit AES-wrapped keys; HSM-backed keys use industry standards. We'll provide specifics in the spec sheet.
[00:06:10] David Kim: About audit logs, does each inference request have a traceable ID we can correlate across systems?
[00:06:15] Priya Nair: Yes, we emit request IDs, span traces for calls, and can forward them to your tracing backend. We include model version, region, and node ID. You can tie that back to your logs.
[00:06:28] Sana Patel: On the 'no training' statement, is there an attestation or contractual clause we can include?
[00:06:33] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can include a contractual clause and add it to the DPA. The clause states that Redwood will not use customer content to improve model weights unless explicit opt-in is provided. We'll have legal send language.
[00:06:46] Carlos Ortega: For Dedicated, is there any metadata that still leaves Redwood's control plane? Like billing or telemetry — could that include customer identifiers?
[00:06:55] Marcus Chen: Billing and account metadata remain in the control plane; you can request that PII-free identifiers are used. Telemetry can be limited; for Private you can host the control plane in your environment. We'll document the segregation.
[00:07:09] Rebecca Miles: We're audited annually; we need to show retention deletion proof. Do you provide deletion logs or proofs?
[00:07:16] Priya Nair: Yes, we can provide deletion event logs and chain-of-custody style export showing timestamps and keys used for deletion. For Private we'll push the same artifacts to your SIEM.
[00:07:28] David Kim: How about backups? If data is backed up, is it still within the region and encrypted?
[00:07:33] Marcus Chen: Backups inherit the same region constraints and encryption. For Hosted we use multi-AZ within the region; for Dedicated you can opt for single-tenant backup controls.
[00:07:45] [00:07:45] Speaker 7: beep, sorry
[00:07:50] Jordan Lee: No problem. Moving to access control — SCIM provisioning fastest path for large orgs; we have SSO session length controls and can enable step-up MFA.
[00:08:02] Sana Patel: Who in Redwood has access to customer data for support? We need a list of roles and justification.
[00:08:09] Marcus Chen: Support access is strictly ticket-based with JIT access: engineers can request time-limited access, it's logged and requires approvals. We'll send the access matrix and justification levels.
[00:08:22] Liam O'Connor: Will that be in the SOC2 evidence?
[00:08:25] Jordan Lee: Yes, access controls and support procedures are covered in SOC2, and we'll point you to the relevant attestations and controls mapping.
[00:08:35] Carlos Ortega: For our procurement, we need to know the retention default values and how to change them via API or console. Is that supported programmatically?
[00:08:45] Priya Nair: Yes, retention is configurable via API and console per project. Defaults are documented. We'll attach sample API calls.
[00:08:54] Rebecca Miles: Can you walk through an emergency data deletion flow?
[00:08:58] Marcus Chen: Emergency deletion starts with a support ticket flagged as emergency, JIT authorization for the engineer, deletion executed and deletion event logged and exported to customer. For Dedicated we can provide direct deletion APIs for customers.
[00:09:15] David Kim: Do you do data minimization on logs? Like strip long context?
[00:09:19] Priya Nair: We support truncation rules, e.g., keep only last N tokens, or strip attachments and file blobs. We'll include config examples.
[00:09:30] Rebecca Miles: A few clarifying questions from compliance: 1) Do you do customer-level isolation of models and caches? 2) Is there any mixing of embeddings or vector stores across customers?
[00:09:40] Marcus Chen: For Dedicated/Private there is strict tenant isolation. For hosted, embeddings and vector stores are scoped to customer accounts; we do not mix vectors across customers and we recommend dedicated capacity for high-sensitivity workloads.
[00:09:55] Carlos Ortega: On the audit log exports — can you produce them in a format that our auditors can ingest (e.g., NDJSON) and include integrity hashes?
[00:10:02] Priya Nair: Yes, NDJSON is supported and we can include SHA-256 digests or signed manifests.
[00:10:09] Jordan Lee: Quick aside: we'll also share architecture diagrams showing the separation between control plane and data plane; that helps procurement.
[00:10:18] Sana Patel: For PHI scanning, will Redwood ever surface PHI in the console or support UI?
[00:10:25] Marcus Chen: The console can display request metadata, but we can mask or redact the text payloads for enterprise customers. By default the console will not expose raw prompt text unless you enable debug mode.
[00:10:38] Rebecca Miles: Is there an option for us to host the console internally?
[00:10:42] Priya Nair: For Private we can provide a customer-hosted control plane option. We'll include a diagram and deployment notes.
[00:10:52] David Kim: Regarding KMS, how does key rotation impact existing cached KV entries that were encrypted with older keys?
[00:10:59] Marcus Chen: We re-wrap data keys with the new key during rotation; we keep a keyring so older wrapped keys can be unwound for reads until TTL. We can provide a sample rotation lifecycle.
[00:11:12] Carlos Ortega: Are there any SOC2 exceptions or open remediation items you want us to be aware of?
[00:11:18] Jordan Lee: Nothing material; we had a low-severity finding around patching processes last quarter which is remediated; details are in the report.
[00:11:28] Sana Patel: One more: how do you handle subpoena or law enforcement requests?
[00:11:33] Marcus Chen: We have a legal process — we notify customers where permitted and we require lawful process. For dedicated/private we can route requests to customer. We'll include the policy summary.
[00:11:45] [00:11:45] Speaker 7: background voice
[00:11:50] Jordan Lee: OK, let's summarize next steps — Jordan will send security pack and SOC2, Priya will schedule the KMS deep dive and Marcus will share audit log export examples. Acme to confirm retention and BAA interest.
[00:12:05] Rebecca Miles: Thanks. Also please include a one-paragraph attestation that "Redwood does not use customer data to train model weights unless explicit opt-in occurs". Our procurement legal wants that exact language.
[00:12:18] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — we'll include that exact sentence and put it in the DPA addendum.
[00:12:24] Carlos Ortega: Can we get a technical deep dive next week? I'm available Tue/Thu.
[00:12:29] Priya Nair: We can do Thursday 2025-11-27 10am PT, I'll send a calendar invite.
[00:12:36] David Kim: For the PoC checklist — we want sample retention configs, KMS BYOK walkthrough, and a small bench to validate latency in EU region. Can Redwood run that?
[00:12:45] Marcus Chen: Yes, we'll run a small bench on dedicated infra and share results.
[00:12:50] Liam O'Connor: I'll look for SOC2 and the BAA template.
[00:12:54] Jordan Lee: Great. Anything else?
[00:12:58] Sana Patel: No, that's it from compliance.
[00:13:00] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, end of call. We'll follow up with the pack within 24 hours.
[00:13:05] [END OF CALL]

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and background noise. Some technical terms were slightly garbled in transcription (KV cache appeared as K-V cash in one snippet), but overall content captured the security commitments and next steps.
